title: AI creation hate
author: Cr34mSoda
selftext:
Hey there Folks !

So .. in the near future, i would definitely want to create my game, and i am good at using AI to create projects in general (Not Slop) because i am currently working on some and currently just finished my ultimate project, which is a gaming related mobile app, and it literally took me a year and half to make it perfect with my own design and everything that it’s almost impossible to look at it as slop.

Anyway, that’s not the point here, the point here is, you do know the immense hate on AI creations whatever it is from a lot of gamers, and it’s seems like it’s a majority. Why do i think that ? Because they forced steam to force (i’m not sure about this one though) to declare what parts of their game is AI.

So my question is, how do you deal with that, EVEN if your game feels so successful and looks amazing and doesn’t look slop at ALL. Heck if it wasn’t for your declaration that it’s made with AI, normal players wouldn’t even notice, but ONCE they do, they’ll pushback and instead hate on it, and fight it.

How do you guys feel or even deal with such issue ? To me, it’s super stupid as long as the game does what it’s supposed to do, with everything delivered and as intended by the game dev NOT by the AI. Basically using AI as a tool more than it is as a someone making it for me completely (which i don’t also see what’s wrong with this as well.)

comments.author: RUSuper
comments.body: Ignore them, focus on constructive criticism/feedback only.

replies.author: Cr34mSoda
replies.body: It’s not about ignoring, it’s about if you have a finished game and put it on steam that you poured your heart and soul into, that people will then see that’s made with AI, they will instantly review bomb it to failure just for that, EVEN if it’s a well made, polished game.

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body:
I doubt anybody will tell you for a simple reason nobody made a game with AI only here and put it on steam, all you see is bunch of prototypes and one shots 🤷‍♂️

I'm in the process of creating Steam page (as soon as my ID is reviewed) so I might be able to tell you in few weeks lol

replies.author: Cr34mSoda
replies.body:
That’s cool dude ! I wish you the best of luck ! 

Yeehh sure ! Ofcourse there are going to be some human elements here and there. But even a single AI element for them is a HELL NO, and for that some really great gaming are failing. 

I played one and LOVED so much, but it got hate just because it was made with AI, and i didn’t even notice it until i read the reviews and later the declaration.

replies.author: RUSuper
replies.body: Honestly I understand even from Reddit alone. I was thinking of maybe setting up a website with game being sold there (if I even get to a point of selling it since it started as a hobby, but turned into something that might be possible to release). Anyway AI hate is actually becoming cringe, I understand hating on slop but hating on anything that is AI just because it is AI... is weird in it's own right.

replies.author: Cr34mSoda
replies.body: 100% agree with every word. The problem is, that’s it’s literally turning into a cult, they’re even hating on the creators themselves and sometimes gets to a point of abuse (i faced that on instagram when i defended the RIGHT use cases of AI and CRITICIZED Ai slop) .. the slurs and insults i received is awful. Need to remind that i was just DEFENDING the CORRECT use cases of it.

yes.  it is.

replies.author: BrettEPierce
replies.body: If you use AI to assist with coding, how would Steam even know? Are people just declaring out of fear?

replies.author: Cr34mSoda
replies.body: I don’t know how it works, but i think probably just out of fear OR maybe steam’s got a system to spot AI code or something ? I’m not really sure .. but if you scroll down in different steam games pages, you’ll see a section for AI disclosure/declaration.

replies.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
replies.body: Steams new policy no longer requires you to disclose AI assisted coding. The only thing you have to disclose is stuff the end user can visibly see or hear like art assets or music.

replies.author: Cr34mSoda
replies.body: That’s still huge though. I for one, don’t know how to draw, paint, create 3D environments .. etc, so i use AI to create them for me, and spend time to do so, so it doesn’t turn out like slop, and people wouldn’t even notice that it’s AI, only for that disclosure to ruin it for me by disclosing what doesn’t really matter. (That was a hypothetical situation, not actually me spending that time) just trying to make my point here.

replies.author: Upstairs_Tone_4227
replies.body:
I hear you. I can say as someone who is on Reddit too much, sentiment is shifting even here. A year ago the AI hate was very widespread but now you see a lot more nuanced takes like “it’s a tool and it matters more how the person uses it”. Part of that is because AI has gotten a lot better too. 

I think we need to get to the point where AI slop isn’t constantly being thrown into people feeds because that is what causes most of the casual hate IMO. That bottom tier of slop gives AI an unfair perception in the market. Even still, people are not blind to quality. If they see something that looks and plays well, they will not care. We just haven’t gotten to the point where genuinely good games using AI have been released.

I remember one of those games was Crimson desert. comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
I don't think AI use disclosure is a bad thing, even though I find the antis to be cringe.

I've been working on an open source "LLM Facts" disclosure standard label that reports what models were used, what percentage of project files were AI-assisted, and an approximation of token use.

I think that being transparent about AI tool use helps with trust.

replies.author: Cr34mSoda
replies.body: Maybe you’re right, but i feel like these pieces of info isn’t important to disclose. Because just like any piece of software, you don’t disclose your tech stack to EVERY consumer UNLESS they asked. A consumer would only care for the end result, which is the product.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
I think in this cultural, political and legal environment, assuming AI tools are just another part of the tech stack is a little too willfully naive.  That's why I'd disagree somewhat.  

Even if that's technically true, I think many people today do want to know how AI was used and how that relates to energy costs and whatnot, so having a standard is a better middle ground than... Either nothing, which carries trust issues for some, or everyone writing their own cringey blurb, or platforms implementing various blue check marks and such.

replies.author: Cr34mSoda
replies.body: You’rr correct on that .. i am convinced what i said is right, but what you said is reality, so i’d have to agree with you on that.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body: I agree with you, too.  I think you are right, but just on a technical, factual layer.  The social perception layer is, you know, a bit fuzzy at times... even though it influences real legal policy.

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body:
Well, you really cannot tell the total token usage, but I really like this idea! 

I think the transparency would help with thrust.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
It's true, you can't, at least not in this early iteration.  It's all estimated based on averages, with an option for users to manually input.

I do ultimately want to make some kind of hook that allows token reporting as development occurs.

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body: Well, I see at our company my usage in daily basis and this is true for all companies we have charts about usage etc. we see it per model, but exactly measuring from the result is basically impossible, because it not counts the iterations.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
[https://aitransparencyindex.com/](https://aitransparencyindex.com/)

Take a leaf out of the major studios books. Declare your AI use, and just leave it at that. Completely ignore any trolls who try to rail you for it. It's pretty clear it won't affect a truly quality game when you look at the popularity of some of these games and the numbers they pull. These are companies like NC Soft, Pearl Abyss, Konami, Paradox, Treyarch, Ubisoft, Ironclad, Hound13, Stardock, etc.

If someone is going off on your game for containing AI (not the quality of the content) they weren't going to touch your game anyway. You're never going to please everyone. Welcome to putting yourself out there. The reality of the situation is that a lot of games that aren't finding success that are made with AI involved FEEL like AI was involved. Probably because the games that are doing well that use AI don't use AI everywhere. They have experts who know how to make a game properly, and the AI is just bolstering their workflow at parts of the process. The end result still feels polished and consistent. Most people wouldn't even realize all those games in that link have AI declarations -- many of them using generative AI for art and/or text (and most of these probably use it for Code, but steam does not make declaration for code mandatory).  However a lot of the games where people complain about people not wanting to play "because it's AI"... aside from a few malactors, the reality is that people  don't want to play because it feels or looks AI (ie. unpolished or inconsistent.)

AI \*slop\* is hated pretty universally. The data doesn't seem to indicate that AI involvement at its core is, however, even if certain areas of reddit would have you think otherwise.
